Part I — Knowledge Base (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 86, English)
The Conclusion of the Nine-Day Ram Mantra Sadhna: Guru Vachan, Collective Consciousness, and Vijay Dashami

This session marks the formal close of a nine-day Ram Mantra Sadhna conducted during Navratri, held on V ijay Dashami. It is primarily an extended addr ess from Bhaiya to the sangat, bracketed by brief opening testimony/check-ins and a closing collective sankalp (vow/prayer) with a r oll call of names. Standar d (non-conventional-doctrine) number ed format is used, since the bulk of the content is dir ect teaching rather than a r oll-call diagnostic format.

1. Opening Testimony: A Practitioner's Mantra Automatically Changing A sangat member opened by sharing that during her jaap that day (starting around 5:15), the mantra she was consciously reciting ("Jai Siyaram") was accompanied by an involuntary internal repetition of "Parikshit Bhaiya, Parikshit Bhaiya" that arose automatically , without her intending it.

2. Bhaiya's Check-In on the Sangat's Nine-Day Sadhna Bhaiya opened by asking the sangat how they were doing and how their nine-day sadhna had gone, asking practitioners to turn on video so he could see them directly , and remarking that he could perceive from a distance that everyone had attained the tattva (essence) of Sita and Ram during the sadhna.

3. Bhaiya's Humility: "I Did Not Do Sadhna" Bhaiya explicitly denies personally having the capacity to "do sadhna" in the way the sangat did, describing his own nine days as simply sitting in solitude singing his guru's praises (gungaan) — framing what the sangat sees in him as a reflection of the Ram tattva shining through the sangat itself, which he says he repeatedly bows to.

4. Teaching: The Vessel (Paatra) Analogy Bhaiya teaches that receiving Ram tattva is not the dif ficult part — properly holding and preserving it is. He compares this to keeping milk cold in a fitting vessel so it does not spoil; the vessel capable of holding Ram tattva is itself considered great, which he says is why Hanuman ji Maharaj is praised even more than Ram himself.

5. Teaching: A Different Drishti (Vision) Sees Divine Light in Everyone Bhaiya describes seeing a shine or divine tattva in the sangat's faces that they themselves may not perceive in one another , framing this as a matter of perspective (drishti) rather than something objectively visible to all.

6. Announcement: Maha-Y agna Reserved for Purnima, Not Today Bhaiya clarifies that despite rumors of a havan happening today , his guru has given a strict order that the maha-yagna (great fire ritual) will occur only on Purnima (full moon); today , Vijay Dashami, is instead reserved for a maha-mantra jaap.

7. Bhaiya's Account of His Own Nine-Day Isolation Bhaiya describes having gone almost entirely silent and unreachable for the past ten days — not responding even to the Ashaeiynn family , his mentor , or close associates ("Robin") — explaining this was not personal sadhna on his part but simply following his own guru's specific instruction.

8. Teaching: "Ashaeiynn Does Not Run Through Any One Person" Bhaiya states that these nine days proved to him directly that Ashaeiynn's functioning does not rest in any single individual's hands — that a higher governing power runs it, and this became evident to him personally during this period.

9. On Bhaiya Japping on Everyone's Behalf Bhaiya reports that, per what he understood from his guru's circle, every practitioner did their own personal sadhna and received their own individual results, but Bhaiya additionally performed jaap specifically on behalf of the whole sangat during this period, per his guru's arrangement — while asking that this not be framed as anything to credit him personally for .

10. Cor e Teaching: What Bhakti Actually Gives You Bhaiya teaches that bhakti's primary gift is direction (disha) and perspective (drishtikon) — not automatically shakti (power), siddhi, or samriddhi (prosperity), which belong to a separate, later stage. Guru protects you; siddhis (your "companions") entertain/occupy you; mantra is your strength; and love (prem) is your ishta (chosen deity) — living from this understanding is described as setting a devotee apart from others, physically and astrally .

1 1. Personal Anecdote: "Just Four Malas, Eleven Days" Bhaiya recounts that upon first arriving at his own path, he asked his guru how many "attacks" were directed at them and what should be done in response. His guru showed him the situation and then instructed him to do just four rounds of mala (japa) daily for eleven days on a specific sankalp (vow) — even though Bhaiya reports that clarity ("sab kuch saaf ho gaya") came to him within the very first mala.

12. Teaching: Why the Guru's Fixed Instruction Matters Mor e Than Self-Dir ected Practice Bhaiya explains that if left to his own judgment after that first mala's clarity , he might have impulsively done hundreds of malas instead of four — and that the guru's deliberately bounded instruction (four malas, eleven days) was itself a form of protection and discipline, illustrating why following a guru's specific word (guru vachan) is valued over open-ended self-determined practice, however sincere.

13. Teaching: The "Two Steps, Then a Br eaker" Metaphor Bhaiya describes the guru's guidance during sadhna as a rhythm — walk two steps, then a "breaker" (obstacle/pause) arrives requiring a "jump," then two more steps, then another breaker , then sometimes stepping back and waiting fifteen minutes before continuing — describing this paced, guided rhythm as what bhakti and this practice are fundamentally about.

14. Teaching: Why Collective Practice Matters (Collective Consciousness) Bhaiya explains that while anyone can chant any mantra alone at home, gathering together under one name, one tattva, one mantra, and one guru parampara connects the group to a higher - dimensional power ("collective consciousness") capable of guiding practitioners in ways solitary practice cannot — this collective rhythm, not devotion to any individual person, is why the group gathering matters.

15. Clarification: Sit for Your Own Guru, Not "For Ashaeiynn" or "For Bhaiya" Bhaiya explicitly instructs practitioners not to frame their sitting/practice as being done "for Ashaeiynn" or "for Bhaiya" — ur ging them instead to sit for their own Ram, their own guru, cautioning that devotion framed around him personally will not sustain itself over time.

16. Anecdote: Krishna and Arjuna's Shar ed Curse Bhaiya recounts that after the Mahabharata war , both Arjuna and Krishna received a curse (shaap) and bore its consequence together — illustrating companionship in consequence as a feature of true divine partnership, of fered partly humorously ("if I got slapped, you'll get half a slap too") and partly seriously to describe how these spiritual forces genuinely support a devotee.

17. Testimony: A Devotee's Cancer Improving with Surr ender Bhaiya shares (without naming the individual) that a woman's cancer improved by roughly 50% after she of fered full surrender (samarpan); when she later loosened her commitment and trust, her condition partially regressed before recovering again — of fered not as blame toward her but as an illustration of how sustained surrender under collective consciousness sustains spiritual support.

18. Teaching: Full Surr ender and "Whose Br eath Is It, Anyway?" Bhaiya teaches that under true, complete surrender within collective consciousness, a practitioner's very breath is described as no longer being fully "their own" — governed instead by the higher power they've surrendered to — and it is at that point, he says, that real "magic" happens through a devotee's hands.

19. Teaching: Pr otection Earned Through Honoring Guru's Word Bhaiya tells the sangat that by honoring their guru's word (guru vachan) through these nine days, they are now shining in a way disproportionate to the sadhna's apparent scale — and that anyone who
might otherwise confront or challenge them will now find themselves contending with the guru's power actively working around the sangat, rather than with the individual alone.

20. The Closing Collective Sankalp (V ow/Prayer) Bhaiya leads the sangat in a formal collective prayer addressed to Hanuman ji Maharaj, invoking Parikshit (of Ashaeiynn) as witness, submitting the sangat's jaap at Hanuman ji's feet, and requesting to be included in Bhaiya's own sankalp, asking for increased mantra shakti, bhaav shakti, and grahan shakti (receptive power), and to be made a humble servant at Hanuman ji's feet.

21. Closing Roll Call Following the collective prayer , Bhaiya reads out a long list of individual practitioner names to formally include them in the sankalp being of fered — a name-inclusion roll call rather than an individual diagnostic reading.
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

This session marks the formal close of a nine-day Ram Mantra Sadhna held during Navratri, concluding on Vijay Dashami. Bhaiya explicitly frames his own nine days as guru-obedience (sitting in solitude per his guru's instruction) rather than personal sadhna, and repeatedly redirects credit away from himself toward the sangat's own ef fort and the guru parampara. Per this teaching's guru, the maha-yagna (great havan) is reserved strictly for Purnima, not Vijay Dashami; today's practice instead centers on maha-mantra jaap. Core teaching: bhakti's primary gift is direction and perspective, not automatically power , siddhi, or prosperity; guru protects, siddhis entertain, mantra is strength, and love is one's ishta. The "four malas, eleven days" anecdote illustrates that following a guru's specific bounded instruction is valued over openended self-directed practice, even when personal clarity comes quickly . Collective group practice under one guru parampara is taught to connect practitioners to a "collective consciousness" — a higher guiding power inaccessible through solitary home practice alone. Practitioners are explicitly told to direct their devotion toward their own guru/Ram, not toward Ashaeiynn or Bhaiya personally . The session closes with a formal collective sankalp invoking Hanuman ji Maharaj, followed by a roll call of practitioner names included in that vow . Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .
Part II — Q&A Pairs (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Q&A Pairs (Session 86, English)
The Conclusion of the Nine-Day Ram Mantra Sadhna: Guru Vachan, Collective Consciousness, and Vijay Dashami
User-style questions with answers gr ounded in this Ashaeiynn session marking the close of a nine-day Ram Mantra Sadhna, held on V ijay Dashami.

Q1. What occasion does this session mark? A: Per this teaching, this session marks the formal conclusion of a nine-day Ram Mantra Sadhna conducted during Navratri, held on Vijay Dashami (the tenth day , marking the festival's close).

Q2. What unusual experience did a practitioner shar e about her mantra at the session's opening? A: Per this teaching's live testimony , a practitioner shared that while consciously reciting "Jai Siyaram" during jaap that day , an involuntary internal repetition of "Parikshit Bhaiya, Parikshit Bhaiya" arose automatically alongside it, without her intending it.

Q3. Does Bhaiya claim to have personally performed sadhna during these nine days? A: No — per this teaching, Bhaiya explicitly denies having personally "done sadhna" in the way the sangat did, describing his own nine days as simply sitting in solitude singing his guru's praises, per his guru's specific instruction.

Q4. What is the "vessel" (paatra) analogy Bhaiya uses in this teaching? A: Per this teaching, receiving Ram tattva is compared to receiving milk — the harder part is not obtaining it but properly preserving it, like keeping milk cold in a suitable vessel; the vessel capable of holding Ram tattva is itself considered great, which this teaching of fers as the reason Hanuman ji Maharaj is praised even more than Ram.

Q5. Will there be a maha-yagna (gr eat havan) on Vijay Dashami, per this teaching? A: No — per this teaching, Bhaiya's guru gave a strict order that the maha-yagna will occur only on Purnima (full moon), not on Vijay Dashami; today's practice instead centers on a maha-mantra jaap.

Q6. Why was Bhaiya unr eachable for the past several days, per this teaching? A: Per this teaching, Bhaiya describes having gone almost entirely silent and unreachable — even to the Ashaeiynn family , his mentor , and close associates — for roughly ten days, explaining this was not a personal choice but obedience to a specific instruction from his own guru.

Q7. What did Bhaiya say he personally learned during these nine days about how Ashaeiynn functions? A: Per this teaching, Bhaiya states these nine days proved to him directly that Ashaeiynn does not run through any single individual's ef fort or control, but through a higher governing power — a realization he says became concrete evidence to him personally during this period.

Q8. Did Bhaiya perform jaap on behalf of the whole sangat during this sadhna? A: Per this teaching, yes — while each practitioner did their own personal sadhna and received their own individual results, Bhaiya additionally performed jaap specifically on behalf of the whole sangat during this period, per his guru's arrangement, though he asks this not be treated as something to personally credit him for .

Q9. What does this teaching say bhakti primarily gives a devotee? A: Per this teaching, bhakti's primary gift is direction (disha) and perspective (drishtikon) — not automatically shakti (power), siddhi, or samriddhi (prosperity), which belong to a separate, later stage of spiritual development.

Q10. In this teaching's framework, what r oles do guru, siddhi, mantra, and love each play? A: Per this teaching, the guru protects you, your siddhis are companions that occupy/entertain you, your mantra is your strength (shakti), and love (prem) is your ishta (chosen deity) — living from this framework is described as setting a devotee apart from others.

Q1 1. What is the "four malas, eleven days" anecdote Bhaiya shar es about his own early practice? A: Per this teaching, Bhaiya recounts asking his guru about spiritual attacks directed at him early in his path; his guru showed him the situation and then instructed him to do only four rounds of mala daily for eleven days on a specific vow — even though Bhaiya reports gaining full clarity within the very first mala.

Q12. Why does this teaching emphasize following the guru's specific, bounded instruction rather than one's own judgment? A: Per this teaching, Bhaiya explains that had he followed his own judgment after that first mala's clarity , he might have impulsively done hundreds of malas instead of four; the guru's deliberately limited instruction was itself protective and disciplined, illustrating why guru vachan (the guru's word) is valued over open-ended self-directed practice.

Q13. What is the "two steps, then a br eaker" metaphor in this teaching? A: Per this teaching, Bhaiya describes guided spiritual progress as a paced rhythm — walking two steps, encountering a "breaker" requiring a jump, walking two more steps, sometimes stepping back and pausing for a period before continuing — framing this guided, non-linear pacing as central to what bhakti and this practice involve.

Q14. Why does this teaching emphasize collective (gr oup) practice over solitary home practice? A: Per this teaching, while anyone can chant any mantra alone at home, gathering together under one name, tattva, mantra, and guru parampara connects the group to a higher -dimensional "collective consciousness" capable of guiding practitioners in ways solitary practice cannot access alone.

Q15. Does this teaching instruct practitioners to devote themselves to Ashaeiynn or to Bhaiya personally? A: No — per this teaching, Bhaiya explicitly instructs practitioners to sit and practice for their own guru and their own Ram, not "for Ashaeiynn" or "for Bhaiya," cautioning that devotion centered on him personally will not sustain itself over time.

Q16. What does the Krishna-and-Arjuna curse anecdote illustrate in this teaching? A: Per this teaching, Bhaiya recounts that after the Mahabharata war , both Krishna and Arjuna received a curse and bore its consequence together — illustrating, partly humorously and partly seriously , the companionship in consequence that characterizes a genuine divine partnership.

Q17. What testimony does this teaching shar e about a devotee's cancer and surr ender? A: Per this teaching, Bhaiya shares (without naming the individual) that a woman's cancer improved by roughly 50% after full surrender; when her commitment and trust later loosened, her condition partially regressed before recovering again — of fered as an illustration of how sustained surrender under collective consciousness sustains spiritual support, not as blame toward her .

Q18. What does this teaching mean by saying "your breath is not your own" under full surrender? A: Per this teaching, under true, complete surrender within collective consciousness, a practitioner's breath is described as governed by the higher power they've surrendered to rather than by themselves alone — and it is at that point, per this teaching, that genuine "magic" happens through a devotee's hands.

Q19. What pr otection does this teaching say the sangat has earned by honoring their guru's word during these nine days? A: Per this teaching, Bhaiya tells the sangat that having honored guru vachan through these nine days, anyone who might otherwise confront or challenge them will now find themselves contending with the guru's power actively working around the sangat, rather than with the individual practitioner alone.

Q20. How does this session close? A: Per this teaching's live practice, the session closes with a formal collective sankalp (vow/prayer) led by Bhaiya, invoking Hanuman ji Maharaj and Parikshit as witness, submitting the sangat's jaap at Hanuman ji's feet and requesting
inclusion in Bhaiya's own sankalp, followed by a roll call of individual practitioner names formally included in the vow .
Bot Response Guidelines

Present Bhaiya's repeated redirection of credit away from himself (Q3, Q6, Q8) as a consistent, deliberate rhetorical and devotional stance in this teaching, not as false modesty to be second-guessed. Present the "four malas, eleven days" anecdote (Q1 1–Q12) as an illustration of guru-obedience over self-directed practice, specific to this tradition's framework — not as general life advice about restraint. Present the cancer testimony (Q17) with care and without amplification — it is of fered in this teaching as an illustration of sustained surrender , not as a medical claim, and should not be generalized into guidance about foregoing medical treatment. Reinforce Q15 (devotion directed at one's own guru/Ram, not at Ashaeiynn or Bhaiya personally) when relevant, as it reflects this tradition's own explicit self-correcting stance against personality-centered devotion. Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .
Part III — Curated Conversational Q&A (Hinglish)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Curated Conversational Supplement (Session 86, Hinglish)
Nau Din ki Ram Mantra Sadhna ka Samapan: Vijay Dashami

Note: yeh session mostly Bhaiya ka ek extended addr ess/teaching tha jo nau-din ki sadhna ke samapan par diya gaya, formal collective sankalp aur names ke r oll call ke saath khatam hua. Genuine live sangat back-and-forth is session mein limited tha — neeche sirf woh chand exchanges include kiye gaye hain jo opening mein genuinely hue.

Sangat bahan (apna anubhav shar e karte hue): सेकंड चरण में आपका नाम आ रहा था ऑटोमेिटकली। आज मैं जब भी सवा पांच बजे स्टाट� िकया तो अंदर जय िसयाराम का जाप बोल रहे थे, लेिकन अंदर परीिक्षत भैया परीिक्षत भैया ऐसा चालू हो गया था ऑटोमेिटकली।
Bhaiya: अरे भाई, मैंने इनको बोला नहीं है। नहीं नहीं, आपने नहीं बोला, ऑटोमेिटकली चालू हो गया।

Yeh exchange isliye include kiya gaya kyunki yeh session ka opening testimony hai — ek genuinely unusual, spontaneous experience jo practitioner khud confused/surprised hoke shar e kar rahi hai, aur Bhaiya bhi halke mazaak ke saath acknowledge karte hain.
Sangat bahan (r egr et shar e karte hue): जय िसयाराम भैया। मेरे साथ बहुत बुरी बनी भाई। पेमेंट भी कर दी और िफर मैं अटेंड भी नहीं कर पाई।
Bhaiya: चलो, जब बाबा की इच्छा।

Yeh exchange isliye include kiya gaya kyunki yeh ek r elatable, honest moment hai — koi practitioner disappointment shar e kar rahi hai, aur Bhaiya ka r esponse ek gentle, non-judgmental acceptance dikhata hai jo shayad doosr e practitioners ko bhi comfort de sakta hai jab unka plan expectation ke mutabik na chale.

Bhaiya (apni humility explain karte hue): मैं साधना क�ं इतनी मेरी क्षमता नहीं है। मैं तो बस एकांत में बैठकर गुरु का गुणगान कर रहा था। आप लोगों ने साधना की है, हमने नहीं की और आपके चेहरे पर यह सब िदखाई देता है।

Yeh exchange isliye include kiya gaya kyunki yeh Bhaiya ka ek genuinely humble moment hai — public r oop se apni khud ki simitata maanna aur cr edit poori tarah sangat ko dena, jo unke overall teaching style ko r eflect karta hai.

Note on curation: is session ka core content — bhakti, guru vachan, aur collective consciousness par extended teaching — Part I mein already detail mein cover ho chuka hai. Yahan Part III mein sirf woh chand genuine live exchanges include kiye gaye hain jo session ki shuruaat mein hue; baaki poora session lar gely ek monologue address, formal sankalp, aur names ka roll call tha.
